lit-myth-04-c4.text: Anindita Basu (2016). Ramayana. World History Encyclopedia.
lit-myth-04-c4.quote: When the brothers were out pursuing the deer, Ravana arrived, abducted Sita, placed her in his flying chariot, and flew through the skies to Lanka.
lit-myth-04-c4.claim: The demon king Ravana abducts Sita.

lit-myth-05-c2.text: Joshua J. Mark (2016). Egyptian Book of the Dead. World History Encyclopedia.
lit-myth-05-c2.quote: The Egyptian Book of the Dead is a collection of spells which enable the soul of the deceased to navigate the afterlife.
lit-myth-05-c2.claim: The 'Book of the Dead', actually a collection of funerary spells, guided souls through the underworld trial.

lit-myth-03-c1.text: Joshua J. Mark (2021). Ragnarök: The Cataclysmic Battle of Norse Mythology. World History Encyclopedia.
lit-myth-03-c1.quote: the compilation known as the Codex Regius ("King’s Book", written c. 1270), some dating to the 10th century and included in the Poetic Edda
lit-myth-03-c1.claim: The two main sources: The Poetic Edda: a collection of Old Norse poems preserved in a 13th-century Icelandic manuscript (the Codex Regius).

lit-myth-03-c2.text: Joshua J. Mark (2021). Ragnarök: The Cataclysmic Battle of Norse Mythology. World History Encyclopedia.
lit-myth-03-c2.quote: the birth of the gods of Asgard (the Aesir) and the creation of the Nine Realms of Norse cosmology
lit-myth-03-c2.claim: Notable worlds: Asgard: realm of the Aesir gods.

lit-myth-04-c1.text: Joshua J. Mark (2020). Bhagavad Gita. World History Encyclopedia.
lit-myth-04-c1.quote: The work is traditionally attributed to the sage Vyasa
lit-myth-04-c1.claim: The Mahabharata: traditionally attributed to Vyasa.
